 Omaha-area experts address daylight saving time assumptions 
 Many people assume the extra hour means more sleep and that daylight saving time helps farmers. By Brenna Kiefner Published : Oct. 29, 2026 at 5:09 PM CDT | Updated : 3 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google OMAHA, Neb. (WOWT) - Clocks fall back one hour at 2 a.m. Sunday, Nov. 1, and a Boys Town pediatrician and the Nebraska Farm Bureau are addressing common assumptions about the time change.
 Many people assume the extra hour means more sleep and that daylight saving time helps farmers.
 Extra hour does not guarantee more sleep
 Dr. Clara Brown, a pediatrician at Boys Town, said the body does not always adjust to the extra hour.
 “It’s almost like experiencing like a little bit of jet lag without really leaving your house,” Brown said.
 For parents, the time change can mean early-morning wake-ups or bedtime struggles. Brown said families can start making small changes now.
 For this time change, Brown said, that means “having your child’s bedtime pushed back by about 15 minutes a night for the next few nights, if you can start that tonight.”
 Farm Bureau on farming and the clock
 The Nebraska Farm Bureau said the relationship between farming and the clock is not what many people assume.
 “Given modern agriculture, modern machinery with the lights that we have, GPS technology, I don’t know that it is as vital as maybe it once was in terms of daylight and how that works,” said Jordan Dux, senior director of national affairs for the Nebraska Farm Bureau.
 Dux said the Farm Bureau has a preference on the future of the clock change.
 “We don’t care which one we pick. We just want it to stay the same,” Dux said.
 Adjusting to the time change
 Experts say it can take a few days for young children to adjust to the time change. Brown said that if sleep problems continue for more than a week or two, it is worth checking in with a child’s pediatrician.
 DAYLIGHT SAVING TIME
 Daylight saving time ends on Halloween night 
 Some will use the extra hour to get a little extra sleep. Others will take advantage of the timing and get in on another hour of Halloween festivities.
